surprises.head: Both teams played to type
surprises.body: Nothing in this game strayed far from how these two usually play: the shot share, the quality of chances, special teams, hitting, ice time and goaltending all landed inside their normal night-to-night range.

story.head: The Bruins pour it on late against the Sharks
paras: Casey Mittelstadt scored his 100th NHL goal early in the first to open the scoring for the Bruins. Michael Misa tied it 1-1 for San Jose on the power play less than three minutes later. Marat Khusnutdinov put the Bruins back ahead 2-1 midway through the second, but Kiefer Sherwood tied it 2-2 for San Jose shorthanded later in the period. Michael Kesselring and Mark Kastelic fought late in the period. There were six goals in the third period alone. Early in the third, Tanner Jeannot and Zack Ostapchuk dropped the gloves, and Dmitry Orlov put the Sharks ahead 3-2 on the power play. David Pastrňák, James Hagens and Fraser Minten scored three goals in three and a half minutes midway through the third to turn a 3-2 deficit into a 5-3 lead. Will Smith cut Boston’s lead to 5-4, 27 seconds later, and Will Borgen shut the door with an empty-netter with 28 seconds left.

The Bruins carried the play, outshooting the Sharks 35-27 (26-15 at 5-on-5), and got the result to match. Jeremy Swayman made 23 saves for the Bruins, and Alex Nedeljkovic stopped 29 of 34 at the other end. The Bruins moved to 9-2-1 and climbed into first in the NHL in points percentage, while the Sharks dropped to 6-5-1, fourth in the Pacific.

items.text: David Pastrňák tied Patrice Bergeron for third on the Bruins’ all-time goals list, with 427.
The Bruins have points in eight straight games (7-0-1), the longest run in the league right now.

The Bruins have won both meetings this season.
